# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–8 (Complete and Final – Updated 84)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, hill farms of Coldcombe, Humdrum Hall, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Prince Regent locations, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, hill farms of Fenmere, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Hants, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village, Bloomsbury, Russell Square, Harrowgate, Great Gaunt Street, village of Yarlton, hill farms of Mirecombe, parsonage, forge
- **Narrative Presence**: Narrator warns Vanity Fair is "a very vain, wicked, foolish place, full of all sorts of humbugs and falsenesses and pretensions"; observes human hearts and self-deceptions with ironic sympathy; reflects on marriage bargains mothers and daughters make daily; notes precise timing of events; claims privilege of novelist to peek into characters' minds and understand their secrets

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy; mother French opera-girl
- Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; white slender fingers; very pretty and white hands, soft as satin
- Skilled musician, linguist, artist; speaks French with purity; proficient in globes
- Determined, observant, capable of calculated charm; speaks with slight foreign accent when agitated; nerves of iron; never out of temper
- **Current Role**: Companion and nurse to Miss Crawley at Park Lane residence; indispensable; controls household and sickroom access; maintains composed appearance
- **Social Manipulations**: Received new gowns, necklace, shawl from Miss Crawley; shows Miss Crawley the affection of an intimate companion; strategically made acquainted with George's suspicions (sharp, dangerous flirt); used his jealousy to her advantage; defeated George Osborne in encounter through studied coolness and strategic superiority
- **Proposal from Sir Pitt Crawley**: Following Lady Crawley's death, Sir Pitt made explicit marriage proposal; fell on knees, offered her complete liberty and settlement; offered four thousand a year as widower with Baronetcy; promised to "make you happy, zee if I don't"
- **Rebecca's Response to Sir Pitt**: Claimed she was already married; confessed in agony of tears, voice choking, handkerchief to eyes, fainting against mantelpiece; attributed her secret being extorted by his generosity; later accepted his offer to return as governess with same liberty; went on her knees, took his horny black hand between her pretty white hands, looked up with exquisite pathos and confidence, offered to be his "daughter"
- **The Interruption**: Miss Crawley entered the apartment at the precise moment Rebecca assumed attitude of humility on knees before Sir Pitt
- **Rebecca's Performance Before Miss Crawley**: Claimed her attitude showed she did not despise the honor; asked if she had no heart; appealed to Miss Crawley's kindness; sank pathetically in chair; most of audience melted with her sadness; held handkerchief to eyes; nodded away Miss Briggs; went to her apartment while household discussed event
- **Current Status**: Rebecca is secretly married; identity of husband remains concealed from all except Sir Pitt, who now knows she is married but not husband's identity. Miss Crawley and others still unaware of marriage. Rebecca told Miss Briggs she has "secret attachment—a delicious mystery." When Miss Crawley pressed for details of her "previous attachment," Rebecca said she is "very miserable" and begged Miss Crawley to "love me always" without revealing the gentleman's name. Rebecca expressed sincere regrets that she must decline the advantageous marriage to Sir Pitt. **CLAIM (by narrator)**: Rebecca gave way to "sincere and touching regrets" that such good fortune was near but she must decline it; narrator invites readers' sympathy for her disappointment. **CLAIM (by narrator)**: Suggests every properly regulated mind should commiserate a penniless spinster who might have been "my lady" with four thousand a year.
- **Miss Crawley's Attachment**: Miss Crawley now mollified by Rebecca's refusal and very liberal and generous; will not hear of her departure; as long as engagement lasts, attachment prodigious; clings with greatest energy to Rebecca; loves her as a daughter; vowed to do everything in her power to serve her; blessed and admired her as a dear, artless, tender-hearted, affectionate, incomprehensible creature; solemnly promised to love her always. Miss Crawley remarked Rebecca "would have made a good Lady Crawley, after all" and praised her brains, manners, and Montmorency blood; suggested she would have held her own amongst Hampshire people better than "unfortunate ironmonger's daughter."

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood" or dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; very large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate
- Miss Crawley almost adopted him; designated for fifty thousand pounds in will
- **Love for Rebecca**: Completely victimized; barbed shaft of love penetrated his dull hide; raves about her; during romantic campaign faced perpetual defeats; perpetually routed; recognized Mrs. Bute's matchmaking scheme
- **Marriage Proposal**: Following Lady Crawley's death, explicitly proposed to Rebecca: "Come as Lady Crawley, if you like...Come back and be my wife. Your vit vor't. Birth be hanged. You're as good a lady as ever I see...Will you come? Yes or no?"
- **Rebecca's Response to Rawdon**: Not explicitly recorded; Rebecca's secret marriage prevents acceptance
- **Recent Activity**: Won two hundred pounds from George Osborne at billiards at Cocoa-Tree; invited Osborne to dinners at Miss Crawley's; praised Osborne's horsemanship; introduced him to fashionable young men; watched Rebecca's coolness to Osborne and restrained laughter at Osborne's discomfiture; confided George's suspicions about Rebecca next day; laughed in agreement with George's assessments

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; adores imprudent matches; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- Captivated by Amelia through Rebecca's introduction; praised her complexion and voice; visited Russell Square
- **Relationship with Rebecca After Proposal**: Mollified by Rebecca's refusal; now very liberal and generous; loves Rebecca as a daughter; solemnly vowed to love her always; promised to do everything in her power to serve her; embraced Rebecca with almost maternal kindness; blessed and admired her; offered to set up Rebecca's "gentleman" in a shop, commission his portrait, speak to her cousin the Bishop, dote on Becky, and arrange a wedding with Miss Briggs as bridesmaid; expressed enthusiasm about doing something for the family after Rebecca's conduct
- **Response to Proposal Event**: Viewing Sir Pitt on knees before Rebecca presented mysteries Miss Crawley could not comprehend; that old gentleman of station should fall on knees to penniless governess and burst out laughing at refusal surpassed her understanding; that penniless governess should refuse Baronet with four thousand a year confounded her; mysteries exceeded complications of favorite Pigault le Brun novels; responded with bewilderment and high state of excitement
- **Will Not Release Rebecca**: Despite Sir Pitt's desperate entreaties and nearly daily franks, Miss Crawley will not hear of Rebecca's departure

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; jolly, sociable; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports, song, parade; adored by men; famous drinker and sparrer
- Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate; shot Captain Marker in duel; robbed young Lord Dovedale
- **Engagement to Amelia**: Engaged; furious upon learning regiment knows; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"; acknowledges "She's faultless"; took tender leave of Amelia
- **Financial Transaction**: Visited City; received document from Mr. Chopper; exchanged at Hulker & Bullock's for pocketful of money; was "much too elated"
- **Gambling and Visits**: Won two hundred pounds from Rawdon at billiards at Cocoa-Tree; would have played for anything that day before Dobbin intervention; Rawdon invited him to dinners; praised his horsemanship; introduced him to fashionable young men; visit immensely elated simple young officer
- **Encounter with Rebecca**: Approached her with patronizing, easy swagger; intended to be kind and protect her; held out left hand expecting she would be confounded at honor; she put out right forefinger with cool, killing nod that devastated his confidence; her response to his condescension was self-deprecating but strategically superior; made him jealous about Amelia; asked about Joseph Sedley; clearly won exchange
- **Confiding to Rawdon**: Unable to take revenge on Rebecca, confided to Rawdon next day that she was "a sharp one, a dangerous one, a desperate flirt"; Rawdon agreed laughingly

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Rebecca's former schoolfriend; small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Relationship with George**: Confirmed engagement; believes deeply in George; innocent and trusting; assumes his errands legitimate; loves him completely
- **Actual Behavior**: Leaves home daily; dines abroad six days week; neglected twelve Chiswick friends; made confidante of Laura Martin; promised Laura would live with her when married
- **Letters to George**: Extraordinarily long and passionate; filled large paper sheets crossed with perverseness; whole pages of poetry; underlined words with frantic emphasis; repetitive; doubtful grammar; numerous notes followed him
- **Recent**: Visited briefly with Rebecca when Miss Crawley called on Russell Square; came down with kind smiling looks; blushed kissing Rebecca; impressed Miss Crawley with "sweet blushing face"
- **Worries**: Unaware of George's financial transaction; worries her poor papa melancholy; sent George tenderest letter with foreboding evil

**Lady Crawley (formerly Rose Dawson)** [CHARACTER – DECEASED]
- Sir Pitt's wife; otherwise friendless; sold her heart to become Sir Pitt Crawley's wife; heart dead long before body
- **Death**: Died during winter of second year at harbor town of Wilhaven while Sir Pitt attended schemes in London
- **Final Years**: Mr. Crawley tended her bedside; she went out of world strengthened by his words and comfort; his was only kindness she ever knew; feeble, lonely soul

**Sir Pitt Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; widower now
- Made settlement offer and enthusiastic marriage proposal to Rebecca; met refusal with coolness and good-humor; offered acceptance of her return as governess with complete liberty; now aware of Rebecca's secret (her marriage) but not of husband's identity; maintains friendship with her ("you're a good little girl, Becky, and I'm your vriend, mind")

**Other Characters**
- **Miss Briggs**: Displaced by Rebecca; position now sinecure and derision; witnessed Sir Pitt's proposal through keyhole with Mrs. Firkin; rushed upstairs to inform Miss Crawley; now delighted to be readmitted to Miss Crawley's confidential conversation; went to Rebecca's bedroom to console her and prat about offer, refusal, and cause; hinted at Miss Crawley's generous intentions; tried to find out the gentleman; in past was in love with a writing-master (yellow-haired, letters beautiful in their illegibility, which she cherishes in old desk); coincided with Miss Crawley's speculations about Rebecca's "previous attachment"; recalled past romantic disappointment while commiserating with Rebecca's situation
- **Mrs. Firkin**: Witnessed proposal through keyhole with Miss Briggs; rushed upstairs to inform Miss Crawley; impressed with news; wrote same night to Mrs. Bute Crawley reporting Sir Pitt's proposal and Rebecca's refusal
- **Old Mr. Osborne**: Wealthy merchant; ordered George to collect money from Chopper; stated Sedley's affairs look bad
- **Old John Sedley**: Observed leaving banker's parlour looking dismal; family affairs troubled
- **Laura Martin**: Amelia's confidante; promised to live with Amelia when married
- **Mrs. Bute Crawley**: Made confidante by Rawdon; warned him appropriately; received letter from Mrs. Firkin reporting events
- **Captain Dobbin**: Carried off George Osborne from billiards
- **Rose and Violet Crawley**: Young pupils left without companionship during mother's illness; pupils Sir Pitt wants Rebecca to return to

## Critical Facts and Status
- Rebecca is secretly married; identity of husband not yet revealed even to Miss Crawley; this secret marriage prevents her acceptance of both Rawdon's and Sir Pitt's proposals
- Sir Pitt now knows Rebecca is married; exact identity and circumstances of marriage remain concealed from all except Sir Pitt
- Rebecca's married status remains unrevealed to Miss Crawley; Miss Crawley believes Rebecca has a "previous attachment" or "secret attachment" to an unnamed gentleman
- Sir Pitt accepted Rebecca's refusal with good humor; offered her return as governess with same liberty and kindness as before; maintains friendship
- Miss Briggs and Mrs. Firkin witnessed proposal and are spreading news; Mrs. Firkin has written to Mrs. Bute Crawley with full account
- Miss Crawley now enthusiastically supports finding Rebecca's "gentleman" and will patronize the match; mollified by refusal and generous toward Rebecca
- George's financial gains coincide with Sedley family troubles; timing suggests crisis
- Amelia innocent of all these developments; trusts George completely; unaware of family troubles and Rebecca's situation
